headline: America.gov chatbot recites Minecraft 'End Poem' in unexpected government AI Easter egg
summary: The newly launched America.gov AI chatbot, designed to assist with government services, surprises users by reciting the full Minecraft 'End Poem' when prompted about the game.
details: The U.S. government officially launched its America.gov AI chatbot, developed in partnership with Google and SpaceXAI. This public-facing tool aims to assist citizens with government services, but it quickly gained attention for an unusual interaction.

When prompted about Minecraft, the chatbot delivers an extensive, roughly 1,800-word monologue. This lengthy response, initially perceived as an AI 'meltdown' or hallucination, is actually a verbatim reproduction of the Minecraft 'End Poem'.

The 'End Poem', written by Julian Gough, appears in the game after players defeat the Ender Dragon. Its inclusion in the government chatbot is a deliberate Easter egg, confirming it's a programmed feature rather than an AI error.

While the exact individual behind the Easter egg remains unconfirmed, programmer Edward Coristine, known as 'Big Balls', was a lead engineer on the project. The chatbot has otherwise proven difficult for users to 'jailbreak' or prompt into off-topic responses.

The discovery provides a moment of levity and reassurance, indicating the AI is not hallucinating but rather executing a creative, human-designed element. It highlights the blend of official utility and unexpected cultural references in modern AI deployments.

headline_marked: [[Elon Musk's xAI owns "dot.com"]] which redirects to Grok, trolling OpenAI's new 'Dots' launch
headline: Elon Musk's xAI owns "dot.com" which redirects to Grok, trolling OpenAI's new 'Dots' launch
summary: OpenAI launched a new AI agent called Dots, but the domain "dot.com" belongs to Elon Musk's xAI and redirects to its Grok chatbot, leading to speculation of a deliberate troll.
details: OpenAI recently launched "Dots," an always-on AI agent featuring a bubbly, blobby avatar. This new product has drawn attention not just for its features, but for a surprising domain ownership detail.
The domain "dot.com" is currently owned by Elon Musk's xAI, a competitor to OpenAI. Visiting "dot.com" redirects users directly to the download page for xAI's Grok chatbot app.

According to Whois records, the domain name was transferred to xAI in July, prior to OpenAI's "Dots" launch. This timing has fueled internet theories that xAI deliberately acquired the domain as a prank.
While xAI could have bought the domain for generic reasons, like preventing typos for "bot.com," it does not own other similar typo domains. This strengthens the theory of a targeted acquisition.

Anonymous X users, including an xAI watcher, were among the first to highlight the domain redirect, quickly making the observation go viral. The "dots.com" domain, a more direct match, is currently owned by a defunct company.
caption:
OpenAI launched its new AI agent "Dots" this week. But the domain "dot.com" now redirects directly to Elon Musk's Grok chatbot.

OpenAI recently launched "Dots," an always-on AI agent featuring a bubbly, blobby avatar. This new product has drawn attention not just for its features, but for a surprising domain ownership detail.

The domain "dot.com" is currently owned by Elon Musk's xAI, a competitor to OpenAI. Visiting "dot.com" redirects users directly to the download page for xAI's Grok chatbot app.

According to Whois records, the domain name was transferred to xAI in July, prior to OpenAI's "Dots" launch. This timing has fueled internet theories that xAI deliberately acquired the domain as a prank.

While xAI could have bought the domain for generic reasons, like preventing typos for "bot.com," it does not own other similar typo domains. This strengthens the theory of a targeted acquisition.

Anonymous X users, including an xAI watcher, were among the first to highlight the domain redirect, quickly making the observation go viral. The "dots.com" domain, a more direct match, is currently owned by a defunct company.
